title: Client Clock Estimator
externalChecks: Gate E real-device unsynchronized drift calibration remains EXTERNAL VALIDATION PENDING; clock estimation may be implemented, but perceptual drift/correction thresholds remain provisional
instructions: Implement a pure client clock-estimation module only. Do not add Socket.IO client wiring, hooks, UI, room readiness, or playback control in this gate.
Use the four-timestamp NTP-style formulas: RTT=(t3-t0)-(t2-t1), offset=((t1-t0)+(t2-t3))/2.
Reject invalid/non-finite timestamp exchanges, server-send-before-server-receive, client-receive-before-client-send, and negative computed RTT.
Retain at most the latest 32 valid samples.
For target offset, use recent samples from the last 60 seconds, select up to the 5 lowest-RTT samples, then take the median offset.

The first usable estimate may initialize the active offset directly. Subsequent target changes must slew rather than step during normal operation, initially capped around 1 ms of offset change per second of client time.
Expose serverNowMs(clientNowMs) and diagnostics suitable for the later debug overlay.
Do not encode final drift-correction bands or playback-rate behavior in this gate.
A task is not complete until pnpm watch:gate exits 0 and the GitHub Watch Together Gate is green.
After Gate I passes, stop. Do not begin Gate J readiness/start-barrier work in the same branch.
